title: Separation of suites in strip malls
purpose: To apply the same exception related to fire separations for occupancies in strip malls as allowed for malls with enclosed corridors.
discussion: Many smaller malls, commonly referred to as “strip” malls, do not include an enclosed public corridor as each suite exits directly to the outside. In these cases, are suites of business and personal services occupancy and mercantile occupancy required to be separated from each other by fire separations in accordance with Sentences 3.3.1.1.(1), (2) or 9.10.9.13.(1)? Sentences 3.3.1.1.(1), (2) and 9.10.9.13.(1) specify that suites of business and personal services occupancy (i.e. a lawyer’s or dentist’s office) must be separated from suites of mercantile occupancy (i.e. a retail clothing store) by a fire separation with a fire-resistance rating of 1 hour for Part 3 buildings, 45 minutes for Part 3 buildings in conformance to Sentence 3.3.1.1.(2), and 45 minutes for Part 9 buildings. In a building that is sprinklered throughout, Sentence 3.3.1.1.(3) gives an exemption to the fire- resistance rating required between suites of business and personal services occupancy, fast food vending operations that do not provide seating for customers, and suites of mercantile occupancy. Sentence 9.10.9.13.(2) gives the same exemption in Part 9 buildings for suites of business and personal services occupancy and suites of mercantile occupancy. In both cases for Part 3 and Part 9 buildings, the occupancies are located in a sprinklered mall which is served by a public corridor that is more than 3 m in unobstructed width and does not serve an institutional occupancy or a residential occupancy (see Clause 3.3.1.4.(4)(b)).
variance_text: This variance provides approximately equivalent or greater safety performance with respect to persons and property as that provided for by the Safety Codes Act. In a strip mall, suites of business and personal services occupancy and suites of mercantile occupancy are not required to be separated from each other by fire separations, provided: 1. The building does not exceed one (1) storey in building height, 2. The building has an automatic sprinkler system that meets the requirements of 3.2.5.12.(1), 3. The building has a fire alarm system that meets the requirements of Sentence 3.2.4.5.(1), 4. Each suite is served by not less than two (2) exits which lead directly to the exterior, and 5. The building does not contain a residential occupancy or an institutional occupancy. 6. Where the building contains an assembly occupancy, the suite containing the assembly occupancy must be separated from the remainder of the building by a fire separation with a fire-resistance rating not less than required by Table 3.1.3.1. Major Occupancy Fire Separations.
